Find the value of $k$ for the parabola $y=k{x}^{2}-4x-3,$ shown above.

current_example.problem: The axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=0.25x^2+kx+2$ is $x=-6.$ Find the value of $k.$
current_example.worked_solution:
First, we will calculate the axis of symmetry in terms of $k.$ Then, we will set our result equal to $-6.$

The equation of the axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=ax^2+bx+c$ is given by

$$
x = -\dfrac{b}{2a}.
$$

Substituting $a=0.25$ and $b=k$ into the formula for the axis of symmetry, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =-\frac{k}{2(0.25)} \\  & =-\frac{k}{0.5} \\  & =-2k.\end{aligned}
$$

We already know that the axis of symmetry is $x=-6,$ so we must have

$$
\begin{aligned}-2k & =-6 \\ k & =3.\end{aligned}
$$
